title: Combining Evidence-Based Practices with Staff Education to Reduce the Incidence and Severity of Ventilator-Associated Pneumonia
content: Background/Objective: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in ICUs, particularly in resource-limited settings. The study aimed to examine the association of a combined intervention comprising an evidence-based VAP prevention bundle and targeted staff education with the incidence and severity of VAP. Methods: A quasi-experimental study was conducted in an adult medical ICU, comparing two sequential patient cohorts: pre-intervention and post-intervention. The intervention consisted of an evidence-based 10-item VAP prevention bundle. The primary outcome was VAP incidence according to Centers for Disease Control and Prevention criteria, while secondary outcomes included Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) scores (to assess illness severity) and staff adherence to the bundle. 97 patients were included in the analysis. Results: Implementation of the VAP bundle was associated with a 34% reduction in VAP incidence (68.85 to 45.64 cases/1000 ventilator-days), with 8.5-fold higher odds of VAP in the pre-intervention group (p = .003). Mean SOFA scores during the VAP episode were lower in the post-intervention group (4.45 vs. 9.45; p < .001). Staff compliance increased from 1.8% to 98.3% of days meeting high standards (p < .001), and each 1-point increase in compliance was associated with an 8.4% reduction in VAP odds (p = .036). Mortality was higher among patients who developed VAP than among those who did not (56.2% vs. 30.8%, p = .016). Conclusions: In this resource-limited ICU, a combined VAP prevention bundle and targeted staff education was associated with lower VAP incidence, severity among patients who developed VAP, and higher staff adherence. Further controlled studies are needed to confirm these findings and assess their long-term sustainability.
